REFERRAL REASON
Diagnostic testing for Familial Hypercholesterolaemia

METHODOLOGY
Next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis of LDLR, PCSK9, LDLRAP1 genes and APOB exon 26 was performed. The analysis included all coding exons and splice sites with ±10bp flanking intronic sequences. Target enrichment was achieved using in-solution hybridization capture technology. Sequencing was performed on an Illumina platform with minimum coverage of 30x across target regions.

Bioinformatic analysis included:
- Variant calling and annotation using validated analysis software
- Read depth analysis for detection of exonic copy number variants (CNVs)
- Examination of the LDLR promoter region
- Filtering of variants based on population frequency, predicted pathogenicity, and clinical relevance

RESULTS
Gene		Result
LDLR		No pathogenic variants detected
PCSK9		No pathogenic variants detected
LDLRAP1		No pathogenic variants detected
APOB (exon 26)	No pathogenic variants detected

No copy number variants were detected in the analyzed genes.

TECHNICAL NOTES
This test has a predicted detection rate of 99% for pathogenic sequence variants in the coding regions and canonical splice sites of the analyzed genes. The test may not detect:
- Deep intronic variants
- Large structural rearrangements
- Variants in regulatory regions (except LDLR promoter)
- Low-level mosaicism (<20%)

SUMMARY
No pathogenic sequence variants were identified in the LDLR, PCSK9, LDLRAP1 genes or APOB exon 26. The diagnosis of Familial Hypercholesterolaemia has not been confirmed by genetic testing in this patient.

It should be noted that a negative genetic test does not exclude a clinical diagnosis of Familial Hypercholesterolaemia, as approximately 20-40% of patients with a clinical diagnosis do not have an identifiable genetic cause using current testing methods.
